content:
Ohio Democratic Rep. Joyce Beatty detailed a heated clash with President Donald Trump on Tuesday, after Trump lost a legal battle trying to add his name to the Kennedy Center — and then threw what she described as a “tantrum.”

"I will simply say, this is the most unprofessional thing I have ever witnessed or been a part of," Beatty said Tuesday evening on MS NOW’s "The Weeknight."

"He started with name-calling, everything, calling me an obstructionist, calling me stupid," the Democrat continued. "He said, 'I think you're incompetent.' I said, 'I know you're incompetent.'"

"I would not allow him to belittle me with that type of language," Beatty said.

Beatty, a congressionally appointed member of the Kennedy Center Trust Board, told the MS NOW anchor that on a board video call on Tuesday, Trump singled her out over the venue's renovations. Trump has said renovations would not proceed unless the memorial to the late President John F. Kennedy bore his name.

"He said if something fell from the ceiling and killed someone, he would hold me responsible. I said, 'You are already killing people. We are at war, people are starving. That's what you're doing,'" Beatty told the MS NOW anchor.

"He then wanted to brag about how wonderful he was and knew nothing about me but said I had done nothing, this was the biggest thing I've ever done. And I reminded him he's been bankrupt more times than anyone in the room," she added.

Watch a clip of Beatty describing Trump's "tantrum" here:

The White House told HuffPost in a statement that "for decades, Democrats have let the Kennedy Center fall into disrepair, with leaks spreading, infrastructure crumbling, and a national treasure disintegrating right before their eyes," and said Trump would "restore the Kennedy Center and make it the premiere performance arts venue in the world."

Since the Kennedy Center opened in 1971, four Democrats and six Republicans have served as chair of the center, including Trump during his first term.

The Kennedy Center's board, now stacked mostly with the president's allies, voted on Tuesday to close the venue. Trump wrote on Truth Social that the board voted "nearly unanimously" to close the center immediately, claiming the site was "on the verge of collapse."

But speaking separately to CNN's Kaitlan Collins, Beatty pushed back against the president's claims that the center would close immediately. She said she did not vote in favor of closing, and that other board members "did not vote the way he posted on Truth Social."

Watch a clip of Beatty's interview with Kaitlan Collins here:

Beatty told Collins she believed Trump's call on Tuesday was "targeted toward me" because her name appeared on the lawsuit blocking his renaming of the center. "He picked the wrong person," she said.

"I think anyone hearing a president speak in those terms would find it unbelievable," Beatty said. "He threw a tantrum, like a very immature little boy. I don't want to even call this little boy. It's just very — in my view — very childish, screaming and yelling, and renaming things."

"I am disappointed, but I will not tolerate him bullying me, because that's who he is. He wants to intimidate," the lawmaker said. "He wants to bully because he's not getting his way, because he wants to make this his personal vanity project."
